name: Tuz-Kol, Dead Lake
near: Kyzyl-Tuu and Kara-Koo on the Balykchy–Karakol highway (south shore), km 56–73 from Balykchy; from the highway to the lake there are 12–14 km of gravel road. The lake lies 400 m to 1 km from the shore of Issyk-Kul.
elev: ≈1609–1611 m (geocaching 1609 m, Nomad's Land 1611 m, Baibol 1600 m) — practically at the level of Issyk-Kul (1607 m).
short: A small hypersaline lake near the south shore of Issyk-Kul, separated from the big lake by a narrow strip of land: salinity up to 236 g/L seasonally (as in the Dead Sea), the water holds you afloat, and on the bottom there are healing muds of three colors. A paid fenced area with yurts, a cafe and a shower; 12–14 km of gravel road from the highway.
desc: Tuz-Kol (“salt lake”) is a separate body of water with a shoreline of ≈1.5 km and a depth of up to 11 m, a kilometer from Issyk-Kul, between the villages of Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu. Salinity changes with the season from ≈62 to 236 g/L, so in summer people lie in the water as if on a mattress, and in winter the lake does not freeze. On the bottom and shores there are black, blue and green muds, which people smear on “for psoriasis and joints”; there is no fresh water nearby, and you have to rinse off the salt in a paid shower. Until the 2000s the place was little known, and since the 2010s it has become popular: the farmers' cooperative “Gulistan” fenced off the territory (since 2014 a per-person and per-car fee has been charged by decision of the local kenesh), and yurts, a cafe, changing cabins, toilets and a shower appeared. The approach is 12–14 km of gravel road with bends and bumps from the highway after Kesken-Bel Pass; it is better not to drive down to the sandy shore without 4WD. In 2021 tourists complained of charges without receipts and poor sanitation (24.kg), in 2018 of litter, after which “order was restored” with separate waste collection. The Ak-Sai canyons are 13 km away, so the two are often combined in one day.
guide: Enter the water slowly and don't dive: at 200+ g/L of salt a drop in the eye means a minute of tears, and any scratch will immediately remind you of itself. Lie on your back and lift your feet — here it happens by itself, as in the Dead Sea, and the “reading a newspaper in the water” photo is a must. Take mud from the bottom near the shore, smear it on and let it dry in the sun, then wash it off — only in the paid shower, there is no fresh water at the lake at all. It is better to come in July–August: the water is warmed, and salinity is higher by the end of summer, so it “holds” you more. Bring water shoes, drinking water and cash: entry, the shower and the toilet are paid here, and a receipt is not always given.
see: Floating “lying down” on hypersaline water; healing muds of three colors; a view of Issyk-Kul and Terskey Ala-Too across the isthmus; a salt crust on the shores; yurts; sunset over the lake; nearby — the Ak-Sai canyons and Kesken-Bel Pass.
skip: If you have wounds, acute eczema or you are with small children — concentrated salt burns. If you expect the cleanliness of the Dead Sea with infrastructure — here there are simple yurts, two toilets and a 50 som shower, and reviews say it can be dirty. If you aren't ready for 12–14 km of bumpy gravel road for an hour of swimming.
diff: Easy: a drive to the site, swimming and a walk along the shore; the only difficulty is the road (gravel, sand) and the lack of shade/fresh water.
when: June to September for swimming (the water is warm, salinity rises toward the end of summer); the lake doesn't freeze — it is accessible year-round, but the infrastructure works in season. Peak is July–August, weekends are crowded.
hours: A fenced area of the cooperative; the ticket booth/barrier works in daylight in season; there are no official hours. Google Maps: no hours given (meta).
daytime: Midday to early evening for swimming (water and air are warmed); sunset for photos. The water is cooler in the morning.
how: Along the Balykchy–Karakol highway on the south shore to km 56–73 (between Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu), after Kesken-Bel Pass turn onto the gravel road toward the lake — 12–14 km to the parking area. From Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h, from Karakol ≈3 h. By public transport — a marshrutka (minibus) to Kara-Koo/Kyzyl-Tuu and then a taxi/12 km on foot (inconvenient).
needcar: Yes: 12–14 km of gravel road; in dry weather an ordinary car can manage with careful driving, but to the sandy shore only with 4WD (cars get stuck). On foot from the highway is unrealistic with luggage in the heat.
self: Yes: paid entry, the site is obvious, no guide needed. You can arrange a tent with the owners of the territory (Too.kg).
roadtype: Paved highway; 12–14 km of gravel road with frequent bends and bumps (geocaching: 12.2 km by odometer); the last stretch at the shore is sand, where cars get stuck without 4×4. Too.kg: “poor quality of the last section, an off-road vehicle is needed”.
traveltime: From the highway to the lake 20–30 min; from Bishkek ≈3.5–4 h; from Bokonbaevo ≈40 min; from Karakol ≈3 h. On site — 1–3 h.
stay: Yurts at the lake ≈1000 som/night, beds in cabins 150–250 som (2014, geocaching — outdated); Too.kg: yurts, a cafe, a shower and a toilet on the fenced territory, a tent by arrangement and for a fee. Vera guesthouse at the Salt Lake (video/veratravel.ru, not confirmed). Current 2025–2026 prices are not published; alternatives are guesthouses in Bokonbaevo and Tosor, and south-shore yurt camps.
net: Too.kg: there is a signal, but weak (no date or operator). In April 2026 Beeline strengthened its network in Bokonbaevo; Kara-Koo/Kyzyl-Tuu are not named. There is a signal by the highway.
entry: History: 2014 — 50 som/adult + 150 per car (geocaching); since 2014 by decision of the ail kenesh (village council) — 100 som/person + 150 per car (24.kg 08.2018, Too.kg); 2021 — 150 som/person, toilet 5, shower 50 som, no receipts (24.kg 07.2021). Not confirmed: the 2025–2026 rate (expected 150–200 som/person + a car fee). The fee is private (the Gulistan cooperative).
transfer: No public price lists from carriers to Tuz-Kol were found. South-shore benchmarks 2024: a taxi with a wait ≈1500 som per car (Tosor–Skazka), a car Karakol–Tosor 5000 som; Sputnik8 excursions along the south shore — from $330–430 per group (2026).
bring: Drinking water (there is no fresh water), water shoes, a towel, cash in small som notes (entry, shower 50, toilet 5), sun protection and a hat, goggles/don't rub your eyes, a bag for salty clothes, a sun umbrella.
warn: Salt of 100–236 g/L: don't dive, don't swallow the water, protect your eyes and cuts; be sure to rinse off the salt after swimming. There is no fresh water. The fee at the barrier is private, and receipts are not always issued (24.kg 2021); sanitation is basic. The sandy shore is a trap for cars without 4×4. Mud therapy for skin and heart conditions — with caution.
food: The cafe and yurts on the territory serve simple food (shashlik, lagman, tea) in season; the menu and prices are not published. The nearest cafes are in Kyzyl-Tuu, Kara-Koo and Bokonbaevo; on the south shore — smoked Issyk-Kul fish by the highway.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.3/5, 234 ratings (03.10.2026). Yandex/2GIS/TripAdvisor — listings not checked. Pros: “like the Dead Sea”, muds, views, an unusual experience. Cons (24.kg 2018, 2021; reports): charges without receipts, litter and poor sanitation at peak season, a bad road, no fresh water or shade.
p.sum: A salt lake on the south shore ≈60–73 km from Balykchy: from the highway between Kara-Koo and Kyzyl-Tuu (after Kesken-Bel Pass) 12–14 km of “washboard” gravel (≈30 min), the last stretch is sand. In dry weather ordinary cars get there too, but a crossover/4×4 is better; after rain it is impassable. Without a car — a taxi from Bokonbaevo/Balykchy (≈1500–1800 som) or south-shore tours. Entry ≈150 som/person (2025), shower 80–100, toilet 30 — bring plenty of fresh water, sandals and cash; it is convenient to combine with the Ak-Sai canyons (20–30 km east).

p.season: June–September: warm water, salinity rises toward the end of summer; July–August and weekends — crowded; May and October — cool, services partial; winter — the lake doesn't freeze, but there is no infrastructure. Rain makes the road impassable.
p.budget.economy: ≈2000–3500 som/day: train/marshrutka (minibus) to Balykchy 150–600, taxi 1500–1800 per car (split it), entry 150, shower 100, toilet 30, yurt camp $17–23
p.budget.comfort: ≈8000–15,000 som/person: your own/rented car or a south-shore tour $330–430 per car, Feel Nomad $50 for two
p.permits: Not needed. A fee at the barrier of the private cooperative (“Gulistan”): 150 som/person (2025), receipts are not always issued; the car fee used to be 150 som (2018), not confirmed for 2025.
p.access: With children — yes, but watch their eyes and don't let them swallow the water; for older people — with caution (heart, blood pressure); with a stroller — no (sand); with a dog — salt irritates paws and eyes, not advisable.
